fixer.title: chat: avoid parsing responses twice for screen reader labels

introducer.title: add table count to chat response's aria label

cases.mechanism: Adding table counting placed a second synchronous full-response Markdown lex in accessibility label generation. Because the accumulated response is reparsed whenever a changed chat row is rendered during streaming, CPU work scaled as two O(response length) parses per render and could block UI updates for long responses.
cases.symptom: Elevated UI-thread CPU and render latency during streaming or rerendering long chat responses, with potential interface/animation stutter.
cases.fixedBehavior: The changed code snapshots the response text once and traverses a single `marked.lexer(responseText)` result to count both table and code tokens, reducing each accessibility-label render from two full-response parses to one while preserving label semantics.
cases.evidence: Base line 145 introduced `marked.lexer(element.response.toString())` for table counting while the same method already lexed the full response again at base line 179 for code-block counting. `Response.updateContent` invalidates the cached string and fires `onDidChangeValue`; `ChatResponseViewModel` and `ChatViewModel` propagate that event, and `ChatWidget` accumulates it then calls `listWidget.refresh()`. The list accessibility renderer calls `getAriaLabel` during row rendering. Thus each visible streamed rerender of an accumulated response performed two synchronous full Markdown lexes on the UI thread. The added test directly asserts one lexer invocation per label after the fix.
